intro: Cameroon secured the Women's Africa Cup of Nations crown with a convincing 3-0 victory over Malawi, a result reported by BBC Sport. Forward Marie Ngah Manga played a decisive role, scoring twice as Cameroon lifted the tournament trophy for the first time in their history.

sections.heading: Match outcome and key contributions
sections.text:
The final ended with Cameroon defeating Malawi by three goals to nil, a scoreline that underlined a clear margin between the two sides on the day. According to BBC Sport, Marie Ngah Manga was central to Cameroon's success, finding the net twice in the match. The two goals from Ngah Manga accounted for the bulk of the scoring, and Cameroon added another goal to complete a 3-0 triumph.

While the detailed chronology and minute-by-minute events are not provided in the BBC Sport excerpt, the headline facts are unambiguous: Cameroon scored three times, Marie Ngah Manga contributed a brace, and Malawi finished the match without scoring. That combination produced a landmark result for the Cameroonian national team.

sections.heading: Context and significance of the victory
sections.text:
The win represents a milestone for Cameroon, who have now claimed their first ever Women's Africa Cup of Nations title. The WAFCON is the premier continental competition for women's national teams in Africa and is organized under the Confederation of African Football (CAF). Winning this tournament is a major achievement for any nation on the continent and typically carries both sporting prestige and broader implications for the development of the women's game at home.

For Malawi, finishing as runners-up in this edition of the competition — as implied by the result — is a notable achievement in its own right, even though they came up short in the final. For Cameroon, the trophy will be celebrated by players, staff and supporters as a breakthrough moment that can boost visibility, investment and interest in women's football domestically. BBC Sport's coverage highlights the headline performers and the historical significance of the result.

analysis: This victory can be read as a potential turning point for Cameroon's women’s programme. A first continental title often serves as a catalyst: it raises the profile of the squad, gives players valuable experience under the pressure of winning finals, and can attract greater media attention and funding. Marie Ngah Manga’s two-goal performance in the final, as reported by BBC Sport, will likely elevate her status nationally and regionally and may influence how opponents plan for Cameroon in future tournaments. Analysts might view the result as confirmation that Cameroon is capable of translating talent into silverware on the African stage, while for Malawi the scoreline provides a clear indicator of areas to develop if they are to close the gap at this level.

faq.question: Who won the Women's Africa Cup of Nations final?
faq.answer: Cameroon won the final, beating Malawi 3-0 to claim the Women's Africa Cup of Nations title, according to BBC Sport.

faq.question: Who scored in the final?
faq.answer: Marie Ngah Manga scored twice for Cameroon in the 3-0 victory. The BBC Sport excerpt confirms her brace as a key element of the win; the other goal is not detailed in that report.

faq.question: What is the Women's Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON)?
faq.answer: WAFCON is the premier continental tournament for women's national teams in Africa, organized by the Confederation of African Football (CAF). It brings together national teams from across the continent to compete for the regional title.

conclusion: Cameroon's 3-0 victory over Malawi — highlighted by a two-goal haul from Marie Ngah Manga — delivered the nation's first Women's Africa Cup of Nations trophy. As reported by BBC Sport, the result marks a historic achievement for Cameroon and will be seen as a landmark moment for the country's women's game.
